title: The Night Train to Pillow Mountain
synopsis: A toy train becomes a quiet bedtime journey in a familiar bedroom, with a gentle return to the real pillow.

related_resources.reason: CDC (2026), More Parenting Tips and Activities: use stories and pretend play about places; not a sleep study.
AAP (2022), Make your home a great place to play: allow ordinary objects to become pretend-world props.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: In Ari's imagination, the wooden train grew just big enough for one child to sit inside.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: An explicit reality cue helps the one-narrator listener follow the shift into pretend play.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: These are caregiver/education practice sources relevant to the narrative approach; they did not study this story or establish a causal effect.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: Ari was still tucked safely in bed.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: A repeated home-setting cue closes the imaginary journey without asserting a therapeutic effect.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: These are caregiver/education practice sources relevant to the narrative approach; they did not study this story or establish a causal effect.

source_note: Original fiction; caregiver sources justify only broad age-appropriate editorial decisions, not learning or sleep outcomes, and not imaginary biology or sky physics.
